note: An experiment (GAME_SPEC §13.7, Stage 44) on data/benches/fizz.json: a gas from a solid. 2 g of malachite tipped into 50 mL of 1 M sulfuric acid dissolves in about two minutes at Nicol's rate (2018), its carbonate leaving as 0.009 mol of carbon dioxide, which pushes the flask's air and some of itself into a balloon.
title: Experiment: a gas from a solid

steps.title: Malachite into the acid
steps.text: Pick up the jar, then right-click the flask. In the menu that opens, click "tip in the malachite".
steps.why: The flask holds 50 mL of 1 M sulfuric acid. The jar holds 2 g of malachite, a green mineral of copper carbonate and hydroxide, Cu2CO3(OH)2, as a powder.

checks.text: the malachite is in the flask

steps.title: Close it with the balloon
steps.text: Pick up the balloon in the cabinet, then click the flask.
steps.why: The acid takes the carbonate apart: its carbon dioxide is a gas and leaves the liquid as bubbles. With the balloon on the flask's mouth, the gas that leaves the flask goes into the balloon.

checks.text: the balloon is on the flask

steps.title: It fizzes and fills
steps.text: Watch the green powder go and the liquid turn blue. Point at the balloon to read its gas. Click 10x on the clock to hurry it.
steps.why: Cu2CO3(OH)2 + 2 H2SO4 -> 2 CuSO4 + CO2 + 3 H2O. The acid eats the powder at its surface, so fine powder and strong acid go fast. 2 g gives 0.009 mol of carbon dioxide, about 220 mL: it pushes the flask's air into the balloon, and some of itself.

goal.text: every element, mass and energy unchanged

results.label: carbon dioxide left in the flask
